headline: Council approves Ethical Purchasing Ordinance limiting city spending with companies linked to certain conduct in Israel and Palestine
summary: The ordinance covers city purchases and some investments, and it exempts essential goods with no suitable replacement and sole proprietor businesses. Members also amended the short-term rental ordinance. They approved a $410,037 state grant for the Winter Warming Center at the Cummings School and $2,383,850 from parking meter receipts to lower the fiscal 2027 tax rate.
decisions: Approved and ordained the Ethical Purchasing Ordinance (item 26-1023), limiting city spending with companies tied to certain conduct in Israel and Palestine. Enrolled with 10 in favor.
Approved and ordained an amendment to the short-term rental ordinance, with 11 in favor.
Approved a fiscal 2027 tax shift (minimum residential factor of 84.15) and a 35% residential exemption for owner-occupied homes.
Approved $2,383,850 from parking meter receipts to reduce the fiscal 2027 tax rate.
Approved accepting a $410,037 state grant for the 2026-2027 Winter Warming Center.
Approved $319,694 in city money to run the 2026-2027 Winter Warming Center.
Approved a $46,270 supplemental appropriation for the Hazard Mitigation Plan update.
Approved a $140,831 supplemental appropriation for street reconstruction.
Sent the accessory dwelling unit zoning amendment (item 26-1336) back to the Land Use Committee.
Referred the Block 9, Assembly Square housing tax increment financing agreement to the Finance Committee.
Referred the proposal to repeal the medical panel for firefighters and police officers to the Legislative Matters Committee.
Approved a resolution allowing air rifle rodent control in a Ward 7 residence.
Approved the Emergency Streets Protocol resolution, as amended.
Approved a Finance Committee item (6A2) by roll call.
Approved a Finance Committee item (6A5) by roll call, with 11 in favor.
Approved an order asking the Director of Finance to start tracking city purchases of AI products.
discussion: Ethical Purchasing Ordinance: Supporters pointed to Ballot Question 3, which passed last November. Opponents said the ordinance discriminates against Jewish residents and may be illegal, and said city staff have concerns about its legality.

Winter Warming Center: Members asked how the center will handle street harassment and past incidents. Staff said changes include new staging areas and more support during wait times, and neighbors will get flyers with contact information.
Commercial property values: The Chief Assessor said commercial values dropped $363 million this year, largely from five vacant buildings. The commercial tax rate rises to $19.77.
Right-of-way at crossings: A council member said a constituent was hit at a crossing to the community path in Davis Square, and asked the Director of Mobility to clarify who has the right-of-way.
